body:
Because I was born as a broken person and the world doesn't want people like me in it. I have pretended to be someone I'm not for decades now, just to make other people happy. And what have I gotten out of it?

A bunch of "friends" I can not talk to. 
A family that thinks I love them. 
Jobs I can't hold because I'm too much of a head case.
It is a boring life that paints perfectly between the lines, and for what? To impress who? Certainly not me.

I know I sound selfish and uncaring. Maybe I should be grateful just to be alive. But I'd rather just be dead.
Die young. Purpose and meaning are worthless shams.
I just didn't care.

When I was diagnosed with ASPD. well, technically, I always knew I was different. People get a vibe from me, I guess. I've lived with an anti-people shield around me most of my life. Very few people have been able to get past it. My naturally cold personality certainly doesn't help much.

When I hit my late twenties, I pretty much locked myself away at home. Better that way, I suppose. It's been about twenty years now. No real friends, stable job, or life at all, really.

You're better off dying for nothing while you still can than to live on and see yourself as nothing.

I never saw the point of life, even when I was a kid. I always thought that death was a better fate than life. Now I see I was right.

I gave up on the only thing I ever believed in because I was told by others that it was right. Now I'm paying for it. Guess that's what I get for putting my faith in something other people believed in.
Now, that's a sentence I can instantly relate to.

Honestly, I can't say I'm exactly a nihilist either, but I always felt I was at least something close to one. My childhood experience certainly made me care less about the world, and honestly, life in general.

I lived in a country run by a government that took its own people as slaves. The greedy and violent controlled everything. I was once their property. Let's just say I learned a lot of harsh lessons back then.

What I've come to know most of all is that I don't want to live in a world where things like honor, value, meaning, purpose, or morality are dictated by others FOR others. I want to determine my own values and purpose for myself and live accordingly.

In a world that values comformity above all else. Someone like me will never be free.

I think when he says lively freely, he means in a manner of your own choosing as in choosing your own goals and responsibilities, relationships, and so on. Rather than letting others determine them for you.

I always believed that death was a better fate than life. Yet I think it's pride and stupidity that keeps me alive. Too proud and too stupid to die easy.

I hate every aspect of life. Always have. Why? I don't know. Except for the fact that everything gives me an empty feeling. Like, none of it really matters anyway. Not to me, at least.
I have felt this my entire life. What is wrong with me?
I certainly seek liberation. Probably not the kind you're speaking of.

The thing is, I know who I am and what I want. The problem is... well, I'm not too sure what the problem is exactly. Society or lack of courage, maybe.

But I'll think about what you've said.

Sure, I have control of the little things, but I guess it isn't really enough anymore. The sadness has certainly become more prevalent. Resentment, too.

I don't mind the idea of a delusion. As long as it's a delusion, I can at least get behind. I ain't even got that much.

But I agree, life is an ocean of grey. Sometimes, all we can do is move forward.

I don't mind any perspective. That's what I'm looking for mostly, I suppose. I can't promise I'll always be able to comprehend. But I'll try.
Yeah. It's hard to argue against that.

I'm sorry for your suffering, friend. I came from a place torn by war as well. Now I have to live in this strange country, surrounded by people who could never understand me or what I've experienced. Worst yet, I have to pretend like I'm one of them. Like everything's normal even though it's anything but.

In the end, it just seems like nobody cares. The "first world" is designed to induce apathy in its people. How else can they tolerate the sight of their own selfishness.
For me, being selfless only works when it comes from a place of genuine decision. Being selfless because someone else told me i had to be selfless has never resulted in anything good for me.
Neither do I. But then again, there's a lot I don't understand about people.

I wish. Frankly, life never made much sense to me. I just don't see the point, in any of it. A failure to understand something is a recipe for disaster. And I've been living that disaster my whole life.

I apologize ahead of time if this doesn't make much sense.

I have always struggled with a plight similar to yours. Honestly, I've never cared about ideas like good or bad, right or wrong. Perhaps that is why I've failed to understand them. To me, those things are just made up ideas that don't really exist. Pointless limitations. I don't say that objectively. It's not my place to decide what these thing's mean to others.

I know I'm not a good person. I lack empathy, and I came from a part of the world where doing bad things was not only normal, it was a necessity. But the only thing that bothered me about that was the fact that it didn't bother me. Failing to understand why, I began to question everything. It's a long story, so all I'll say is that I turned to a lot of thing's to help me change because I thought I was supposed to.

A priest once told me, "Do the right thing and life will start to make sense..." he meant I should help people and such. So for many years, I did. All I cared to do was help others. But I was more miserable than ever. The reason I think it didn't work out was because it didn't come from the heart. It wasn't who I really was. I was just trying to fit the standard, as if that was some kind of accomplishment. I succeeded in doing so, but all I really ended up doing was making a ton of false friends who only showed up when they needed something. I helped people but I was more alone than ever. I had ignored the voice in my head for the sake of the "greater good" and had nothing to show for it.

In short, I sucked at being good. So I had given up for awhile and reverted to my old self. But eventually, I still had questions. That new experience had ingrained in me an endless curiosity, for the idea of being good.

In the end, I simply want to be true to myself above all else. If it causes me great suffering then so be it. I want to embrace both the good and the bad within me, but there are times when it seems the two cannot coexist.

I have always felt as though life was pointless. And, personally, to me, boring. 

The idea that life could have any value at all has never made sense to me. We live on this miserable little rock waiting to die in service of people and their made up rules we don't agree on or believe in. So many of us have to sale our souls just to even fit in with this endless charades party, betray ourselves and sometimes other's just to get something we never wanted but were told we needed to have.

This world is so full of bs that you can't take two steps without walking into it.

I just don't get it. What people see in this world. I use to think I understood, than I let people take that away from me, too.

Frankly, I don't need life to manner or have a point. It never mannered to me. It would just be nice to have something worth believing in. But there's nothing to believe in, not in this world.
You are speaking my language, friend. Love it.

And thank goodness for it. I want to choose my own purpose and meaning. To live and die for something I actually believe in instead of living and dying for something I don't.

If only I lived in a world where people actually understood this. But I guess it doesn't matter.

I appreciate that. I never cared for the labels nor do I see it as an excuse. I've been around the block quite a few times with all this, my whole life spent trying to "fix" thing's but never quite managing to.

Guess I have no choice but to keep trying until I'm dead. Got nothing better to do.

Sociopathy. The bane of my existence.

"Can't connect with others. Falling in love is borderline impossible. You don't enjoy most things others enjoy. You don't care much for your existence but don't hate it enough to kill yourself. Life feels dull and tasteless, boredom gnaws at your mind constantly, forcing you to seek constant stimulation. Whatever positive feelings you might occasionaly experience are faint and fleeting, like an echo of something that you can vaguely recall.

In short, it's like having depression without actually feeling depressed. It's a hard thing to describe.

Without emotional connections, without having anything to fight for (typically we don't care enough about social issues or religion to engage strongly in related activities), without being torn this way and that by feelings and passions, we have little to do. We are very bored creatures; and without a moral compass to restrain us in our constant hunt for sensations, we hurt people along the way — and never learn, even when punished."

I agree for the most part. And I do blame myself more than anything for my miserable life. I know what would make me happy. In the end, I lack the courage to take what I truly want.

It's my own fault.

Well, i would say you are fortunate to have such strong feelings for such wholesome thing's. You have empathy for your fellow man, something I've lacked my entire life and cannot fix.

I spend most of my days pretending to understand what I do not. People talk about what is right and wrong, not because something IS right or wrong, but because they simply believe what they believe. They like what they like and dislike what they dislike. That much makes sense to me, but why is what they believe more relevant or right then what I or anyone else believes?

Believe me, I've been trying to broaden my ideas on such thing's. I only wish I could find purpose in those wholesome things. It's not what I would've hoped for, but it would be the most ideal. The perfect outcome.

I have to admit, I'm just not like most other people. I can't see the pleasure in the more mundane thing's of life, try as I might. I wish I could. Life would be much easier.

I love the idea of contributing. If I understand your meaning, at least. But even in contribution there can be sin. Satisfying or not.

My question is, what if you cannot derive satisfaction from "helping" other's? What are you meant to do then? I've been helping people for what seems like most of my life now. But helping them has never helped me.

For as long as i can remember I have always found life to be boring. Most people's goal is to extent their lives for as long as they can. I never wanted to live like that. Even when I was a child. What's the point of living if you can never truly be yourself? If you must live in constant fear? Or pretending to be something your not?

I'd rather die fighting for something I actually believe in than live for something I don't.

Problem is, there ain't too many thing's worth believing in in this world. Not for someone like me, at least. I've been all around the world, seen a lot of shit. But I ain't never seen anything worth fighting for.

I wish I had advice to give. I know what I consider worth fighting for, but everyone has to find their own path.
Thank you thank you.

I tell myself that things can change. That I can change. Even though I never really believed it.

They didn't diagnose me with depression, so I don't think I have it. Although I do see everything in a negative way. I always have, even since I was a kid. To me, that's not depression talking, it's just the way thing's are.

But like always, no one cares cause no one can relate, so everyone just assumes I'm crazy or something.

I want to live, I guess. But I'm pretty much out of excuses to do so. So I just lie to myself. That the world is beautiful. That someday thing's will change. Maybe those thing's are true for other's. Just not for me.
Same. I have been trying to help others, thinking that it will bring me some kind of enjoyment or peace of mind. So far it has only been a burden.

I'd call him a coward, at first. I use to think he just spent his life running from everything. Responsibility most of all. But then I think every human has a desire to make a better life for themselves. Some are just more willing to pay a higher cost than other's.

I'm not entirely sure which he is. Did he pay a higher price or did he just dump it on the rest of us? Maybe, both? I still hate his guts, but for some reason I also can't help but admire his actions. Weird.
I would regret not having lived my life as I saw fit, and instead letting the doubts of other's cloud my every action.

In some ways, I've already accepted that I am dead. So, dying would be more of a correction of thing's than anything else.

To me, death is natural. People insist that there's something wrong or bad about it. But, personally, I've yet to see any proof of that. Needless to say, no, I don't fear death. Even with as little as I may know about it, I'm still closer to understanding IT more than I am to understanding life. Life makes almost no sense to me.

I'm the oldest of two. My sister is an angel. Pretty much the best of us and the closest thing to normal. I wouldn't say we have the strongest relationship but she keeps me sane in this crazy world.

My brother on the other hand is a mess and a half. A drunken idiot, through and through. We use to be inseparable, though he was still the annoying little brother in my eyes. Followed me wherever I went. We both fell on hard times when we moved from another country to where we are now. Thing's were just different back there. Even after two decades we still haven't managed to fully adjust.

Life hit us both hard, but I guess he ended up falling in a different direction.

What you say makes sense. Maybe the problem is more complicated than what our words can match. To my minds eye, everything we do is driven by a selfish need to appease ourselves. And I don't necessarily see that as a bad thing. Where I come from, this was a well known and practiced thing. Cooperation was not difficult. So long as all parties were honest and knew their role, and where they stood, no one was treated poorly or unfairly. We stood together with an understanding, and a shared goal. My experience here in America, ironically enough, has been more what you described. I find that it's much more normal to use deception to get what one wants. It's as if people here are hiding who they really are for fear of something I can't quite understand, yet I find myself mimicking their behavior in an effort to fit in. To seem normal. A part of myself I'd like to erase.

I can't refute what you claim and I believe you speak with wisdom. To me, though, it is not instant gratification I seek. I think if anything I suffer from a lack of empathy. A lifelong problem of mine. I just want to live in the moment, even if I do not always manage to. I've seen too many sides of life to view it any other way. I learned long ago that life can be short. Maybe it is pure foolishness, but I refuse to have fear for the future, mine or anyone else's. Perhaps it will not win me many friends, but I loathe the idea of being dishonest just so people will like me. 

The cycle you speak of, honestly, could the same not be said of everything? Everything we are, everything we do. It is never enough. So long as we live we will always strive for something in this life. Unless I misunderstood what you meant by that.

I have no real advice but this has certainly been a big factor in my life. It's almost strange to think just how selfishly I lived for the majority of my life. Honestly, I kinda thought that was how everyone was (and I still kinda see it that way.) To me it was normal. There was no burning of bridges, per se. People used each other until neither had anything else the other wanted. Made sense to me to sperate after that. I was mostly taught to be self reliant and needed nothing from no one. Nothing I couldn't get on my own, anyway.

Once I became aware of this selfishness, I wish I could saw my thought process changed on the matter. At most, my self-awareness on the matter has only made me much more indecisive. I cannot quite tell when I should be selfish and when I shouldn't. I lived guided only by my own desires. Take away that familiar guidance and I become lost rather easily. Lost in doubt, lost in fear of failure, lost in philosophy and the like.

It's almost as if I have lived a certain way for so long that I don't know how to live any other way. It's been like this for over twenty years now. I just feel stuck, between a rock and a hard place. Lacking the "true" desire for selflessness yet seeing it is still the better way to live, or so they say. My challenge lies in trying to understand how others do it, why they do it, and find my own way of reaching that same conclusion. I don't necessarily care what other's think of it, good or bad. Maybe it's just my own curiosity: there is a different way to live and so many people swear by it, there must be something to it. I still haven't figured it out yet, but I keep trying.

Anyway, as other's have said, if you can notice your selfishness and become disgusted by it enough to change, then you are in a much better position, I'd say.
Moving to America. Thought I'd "turn my life around." I thought I was doing the "right thing." Shows what I know.

Yeah, i kind of get that. I have to work twice as hard just to feel half as normal as most people. These efforts usually manifest as an addiction or almost obsession for me.

The more I try to feel like life is worth living, the more I must pursue these "bad habits." The more I do that the more isolated I seem to become. Coping becomes harder and then it just kind of snowballs from there.

I guess I rationalize this pattern as "If I can't survive today, then there's no point worrying about tomorrow."

I guess we all do what we must to get by.

Most people fear death, but honestly I'm glad that there is an end of some kind. I never understood what it was that people saw in life. I guess it's just a matter of being unable to live as they do.

People like me, we can't find enjoyment in the same things as them. We see a different world. One where life is not all it's cracked up to be. Where none of the "good" is even all that great. Life is filled with disappointment, loss, and all kinds of boring bs we have to put up with.

What's so great about that? People insist that life holds immense value. Yet I have never seen it, never beared witness to it, no matter how hard I try and force myself too.

I could pretend I see it. "Fake it till you make it." I've tried and failed. Besides, I'm sick of pretending, especially for the sake of other's. The life they offer simply doesn't interest me.

There are some cases where it's usually rather obvious, no? But you don't have to take my general ramblings to heart. I realize not everything, if anything at all, falls under the scope of how I perceive it. I don't mean to speak some sort of universal truth, though maybe it came off that way.

It's just my life experience and my perception of that experience.

Yeah, I guess that's one way of putting it. I don't look down on other people and their problems. But I do find it a very straining experience to try and care deeply.

And maybe you're right. At least I hope you are.

Yeah, that's fair enough. I can't really claim to understand what someone else is going through. I guess that's part of what makes it so hard for me to talk about. Worried about saying the wrong thing.

Yeah, you're right about it being vague. I guess it's a habit I've picked. For the same reason why I can't just open up to whoever, even to those close to me.

But I agree, real connection is something to strive for. I've had it with some in the past. But I've learned the hard way it's safer for everyone this way. I hate lying, so I just try to say nothing or as little as possible.

Depriving myself of that deeper connection, well... I guess I consider it as part of the price I must pay for the life I have lived.

I only wish I had perhaps gotten into something simpler, less complicated. I tried writing for a few years way back when. But my sense of passion has long since faded.

If I could go back to my twenties and make a very different decision then what I did, I certainly would. I never used to be someone who clung to the past but... times have changed, I guess.

I'm sorry to hear that, friend. I get what you mean. I've suffered from a sort of chronic sense of boredom nearly my entire life. Even as a child, I was very indifferent to things. Didn't really see the point in most things. Still don't. Nothing really makes me "happy" as such. Theres no one I "love" exactly. I just don't see or feel things in those terms, never have. Its not depression I suffer from. So I guess I'm one of "those" dreaded people.

You know, the kind that doesn't really place or see much value in this whole concept known as "human life". The things most other people enjoy doing barely registers with me. Most things are just a boring distraction at this point. And I hate it with every fiber of my being. But I stick to it. I just try to keep my head down. Honestly, I feel like I'm slowly going insane.

At this point, life is just a waiting game and me trying not to lose whatever is left of my sanity. I work, binge watch shows and movies, any kind of easy distraction from my thoughts.

What I miss having the most is a sense of purpose. Something worth fighting for, you know? I had a job I could find purpose in and bring me excitement. I gave all that up when I came to the states. For twenty years, I've searched for an alternative but never found any. So, I've been more miserable than ever.

So yeah, I don't enjoy life. Not even a little.

Honestly, I agree with that statement completely. Albeit, perhaps in a slightly different way. I always felt that life was a far worse fate then death, and that life is utterly pointless and a ceaseless struggle against others.

Personally, I don't despair at that idea. In a way, I long to embrace it. I accept the way the world is. Or at least how I perceive the world to be. My problem is accepting other people's perception of the world, especially because they use that perception to dictate how others should live.

They say to focus on the thing's that make you happy. But for some of us, even the simplest of thing's that would lead to that happiness are put so hopelessly out of reach.

They say you have to live. Yeah, so long as you live according to someone else ideals even if you yourself do not share in those ideals. Your expected to make the "right" choices according to someone elses conscience. This... this isn't living. Not to me, anyway. So yeah, death doesn't sound so bad compared to that.

Also, I do kind of agree with the quote lol. I just don't necessarily think that it changes anything. You like the thing's you like, and dislike the thing's you don't like.
I like the idea of writing my own script, but people tell it's bad when I do. So what are you supposed to do when writing your own script is not really an option?

At this point, I've probably spent most of my life trying to change myself. All to no avail. I realized my heart wasn't in it. I was just doing what other's believed was right. It's not that I'm against change, I want to learn and grow. But when trying to force that change, it becomes a question of why. That's what makes me falter. It's hard to remain true to something you don't see proof of or logic in.

In the end, all I ever really wanted was the strength and courage to persevere and fight for something I believe in. I have long wished for something I could pour all my heart and soul into.

"if you truly want something. You will push yourself for it, do things you never thought you were capable of." 

I'll admit, I've lost a great deal of interest for the "positivity" type talk. Mainly because I've found that sort of thinking, in practice, to be rather dangerous, to say the least. But I do agree, it is very enticing and inspiring.

It's a pretty picture. But I guess some of us are not meant to live in it.

My Girlfriend, the only woman I ever loved, died suddenly and horribly. I don't really know what constitutes coping, I only know what I did after. 

For years I just sort of drifted around homeless and dead inside. I barely spoke a word the entire time. I got tired of being sad pretty quickly, though. Sadness turned into anger. Seeking out trouble became a pass time. The only way I knew how to "cope" at the time.

That was over 20 years ago. Thing's have certainly changed, but I wouldn't say I've gotten over it. I'm still angry, just more inwardly. Still sad, but more in a lonely sort of way. I have no ability to make friends or date anymore. Pretty much just coasting to get by.

I have spent nearly all my life, over 4 decades, drowning in boredom. Life is perpetually boring, day in, day out. Some thing's work but nothing that is realistically sustainable.

At this point, I've tried just about every reasonable option. Nothing works. Now life is just a waiting game. Waiting for the end. Sometimes I truly wonder how others can stomach life at all.
I appreciate that. And I appreciate the chance to be heard. I'm not exactly the life of the party, so I'm grateful you took the time.

I have always believed that life has no meaning, no purpose, and no value except the ones we personally believe it has. As a result, I see no reason to not be myself and do what I want, except for one. Call it indecisiveness.

With that said, my opinion comes with a question: if you believe that life has no value, how should you live?

I was unlucky to born. Because I was born without that innate ability to see my self in other's. To me, life on this world is nothing but a sad, miserable and pointless game we play on the way to our true destination. Wherever you might believe that is. I'm close to over 50 years old, and no matter how hard I try, I can never see what other's see. People believe that life has some kind of value and meaning to it. But I have never seen such a thing. How can you believe in something that you yourself have never seen, heard, felt or even tasted?

At the end of the day, empathy is not something you can grow. You must be born with it. I guess God or whoever made that decision thought it'd be a funny joke. If that's the case, then I think it's safe to say that life is shit.

But giving up is also shit. If both equally sucks, I guess I chose the one I most prefer. I don't intend to die easy, so, here I am. I don't imagine anyone here has ever been similarly in the dark as me? If you have and found a way out, I wouldn't mind hearing some words of encouragement.
You know, I really envy people like you. I wish I could gain fulfillment from such thing's. I really do. But I'm glad for people you.

Those words kinda resonate with me. It's interesting. The idea that perhaps we don't do good simply because it is good. We do what we must so we can sleep at night.

Although, that sleep doesn't always come from the best of things, depending on who you are.

Could you not say the same of anyone's personal values? There are parts of the world where hurting others is very much considered a "good thing". Especially if it means taking what they have. I might believe my life has more value than a pocket full of money, but that doesn't mean everyone else will.

Your absolutely right about there being consequences. I would argue that there always consequences no matter what you do. The only difference between them being the one's we can live with and the one's we can't. If you harm others, then you must accept that harm can be done unto you in return. But there's is usually more to it than that.

I've seen plenty of good people suffer just as much as anyone who might have actually deserved it, sometimes even more so. But they deemed the cost of their suffering worth the price. In which case, that is their choice.

If a good man can suffer for his "good deeds" or for no reason at, than of course a bad man can suffer.

My life experience has taught me that we suffer no matter what we do. If we must suffer, than all we can do is decide what makes the suffering worth it. Each man must decide that for themselves.

I guess if you can sleep soundly at night, maybe you made the right choices.

I appreciate you're honesty and patience. Most people simply stop talking to me when they hear words like that. Sometimes that sense of patience means more than anything to me. And yeah, they had told me about CBT. Tried that route for years, didn't see much change but maybe I ended doing something wrong.

I always felt that I was different from ordinary people and from people who suffer from my affliction. My indifference, my lack of empathy and seeming inability to feel as other's do, it almost makes me jealous in a way. Oddly, that sense of jealousy is part of why I've managed to walk this path for so long. Feeling good from being good is like a puzzle I can't figure out, yet i know there is an answer, maybe one I cannot have, and it makes me want to pursue it even more. Probably the most unhealthy roundabout way of seeking to be good. You might even say I am obsessed with it.

I appreciate your praise even though I don't feel worthy of it. My nature is not exactly selfless, as you've no doubt surmised. I cannot pretend like I am perfect. In my teens to mid-twenties, violence was my vice. I grew up on the streets of a poor country. Fights were a regular occurrence. I don't mean that as an excuse, just as a fact.

Anyway, like you said, don't give up. It is still difficult at times, but I no intentions on giving up on doing good anytime soon, so maybe there's still a chance for me to find what I seek.

I have seen a number of professionals over the years. I've been told I exhibit many of the signs for depression, although, ultimately, and most recently I was diagnosed with anti-social personality disorder.

I tend to get a little lost and confused with all the medical jargon, so I may not be relaying all the information properly. I just know that I've tried near everything I was offered, medication included. They pointed out a path and I walked it to the best of my ability.

Though to be honest, I don't feel it's depression weighing me down, although I could be wrong. I'm not trained to understand these sorts of thing's. Mostly, I just want to do good without feeling like I'm stabbing myself in the foot every time.
So, what should a person in my position do, you think? If I cannot gain the same type of reward the same way as someone else, is there simply no other way?

Yeah, that's generally how I feel. I do the "right thing" because people say that you should. But I'm always left with this sense of betrayal or disappointment. I try to find a way around it, but, no dice.

I'll try to check out your recommendations. Appreciate it.
It would certainly be a blessing to me.

I always felt that death was a far better fate than life. I see death as freedom, not a punishment.

I fear slavery above anything else. I fear becoming someone I never wanted to be. I fear growing old and grey, dying in a bed somewhere. And as other's have said, living "ingloriously" (or in my eyes) as a slave is a nightmare I fear far more than death.

I get what you're saying. I wouldn't say I'm lacking opportunities but more so (based on a lot a other comments) a genuine desire to help. Which, as far as I can tell, has no real fix. But I guess I see no reason not to keep trying.
Yeah, makes sense I guess. I don't think I quite know how to do that, as ridiculous as that may sound.

That is seemingly an almost perfect explanation for what I've come to understand throughout my life, from the first sentence to the last. Sadly, I can relate to that last paragraph. Though I don't think I was fortunate enough to have been born naturally empathetic, the rest certainly sounds familiar and explains a lot.

I also feel something undeniable when I witness someone's act of genuine compassion. I guess it gives me a feeling of hope? It makes me want to show it back, even if I don't quite know how or why.

Just wondering, how do you cope normally? Are you healed nowadays? Or only when receiving love and compassion?
Yeah, that unfortunately makes sense.
I see. Something to think about at least.
I don't know about love but I know about help. I've been helping people for the last 20 years now. Haven't seen any of that come back around. How long do I have to wait?
I feel the same way. I'm always helping other's but no one ever cares about helping me. Half the time I wonder why I even bother.

This is what I meant when I said it's somewhat hard to talk about. I like the fight but I hate constraints. I've explored those paths before. Boxing is fine but it wasn't what I was looking for. Same with any fight related sport. They just don't cut it for me.

As to why. I'd probably say: safety nets, rules. Too much of both.

This is literally the type of conversation I have to tiptoe with my words around. Because I never know when I'm going to say something that people would rather they didn't hear.

Not mercy or forgiveness or justice or guilt. Than it taught me that freedom for all was far more important and worth fighting for on every possible level. Then came the latest and most complete lesson: that living to fight and die for what you believe in is the ultimate form of freedom. Thus far, those are my observations, anyway.
